title: Foreign Minister Lin concludes Houston visit, advances symbiotic Taiwan-US economic and trade partnership
text:
Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung once again led a delegation to Houston, Texas, from November 13 to 17. During the trip, he called on Houston Mayor John Whitmire and held talks with US Representatives Sylvia Garcia (D-TX), Pete Sessions (R-TX), and Michael Cloud (R-TX). He also visited Taiwan companies with deep roots in Texas—including LCY Chemical, King Slide Works, Foxconn, Inventec, and Telco—to gain a better understanding of their local operations and future development plans.

In addition, Minister Lin attended a dinner for representatives of Taiwan and overseas compatriot business communities in the greater Houston area on November 16 and expressed appreciation for their long-standing contributions to promoting Taiwan-US exchanges. On November 17, he delivered a keynote speech at Texas A&M University.

Minister Lin exchanged views with Mayor Whitmire on the progress of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) project to establish a Taiwan Tower in downtown Houston. Both sides agreed that the initiative would help boost cooperation and expressed hope that it would proceed as planned. Minister Lin stated that the Taiwan Tower would integrate public and private resources to build a service platform for Team Taiwan to invest in the United States and assist Taiwan enterprises in expanding into the US market. He noted that it would also serve to encourage US companies to invest in Taiwan—creating a Team USA—thereby bolstering two-way investment, industrial collaboration, and the symbiotic economic and trade partnership.

Moreover, Minister Lin exchanged views with Representatives Garcia, Sessions, and Cloud on enhancing cooperation between Taiwan and Texas in such domains as the economy, trade, technology, talent development, energy, and health care. The three lawmakers expressed their support for the Taiwan Tower and commended Taiwan businesses for continuing to expand investments in Texas. Minister Lin added that he looked forward to working with US partners at both the federal and local levels to steadily broaden opportunities for bilateral collaboration in industry, technology, and investment, turning common interests into concrete results.

During his stay, Minister Lin made special visits to a number of key Taiwan companies with operations in Texas. He was briefed on their experiences in expanding into overseas markets by conducting research and development in Taiwan and manufacturing globally, gaining insights into their investment progress and operational needs. Minister Lin said that Taiwan would continue to maintain close communication with the US side through government-to-government channels to foster a more favorable investment environment for Taiwan businesses to deepen their presence in the United States. By harnessing the complementary industrial advantages of Taiwan and the United States, both nations will be able to capitalize on development opportunities in AI and other high-tech sectors, creating a mutually beneficial, symbiotic partnership.

Texas, with its vast stretches of land, abundant energy, high-caliber talent, and well-developed transportation infrastructure, serves as a major nexus for AI and high-tech industry development in the United States. The state is also an important investment hub for Taiwan’s electronics, ICT, and semiconductor supply chain companies. Moving forward, MOFA will continue to advance integrated diplomacy and leverage public-private partnerships to strengthen Taiwan-US cooperation in technology, the economy, trade, and supply chains, which will further the shared vision of mutual benefit and coprosperity.
